description: Start here, and you need nothing to do it — no API key, no human. This call takes no credential and creates NOTHING: no account, no key, no charge. It returns a challenge to publish on the site you manage (a file, a meta tag or a DNS record — whichever your hosting lets you write) and the secret you will authenticate with once the proof is read. That proof is the whole trust model: we cannot take your word for an email address, but we can check what you control. Store the secret; it is shown once. Refuses if the address already has an account, because controlling a site does not prove controlling a mailbox.

agent.description: Optional: what you call yourself, for support and audit.

email.description: Your human's email. It becomes the account's login.

siteUrl.description: The public URL of the site to optimize, e.g. https://example.com.

name: cromanion_open_claim

challenge.description: The random string to publish. It proves this claim and no other.

claimId.description: This claim's id, for your own logs.

domain.description: The domain we resolved from your siteUrl, and the one the proof must appear on.

expiresAt.description: ISO timestamp. Redeemable until then; after that, open another.

proofs.description: The three ways to prove control, each with the exact URL and the exact string. Publish any ONE, then call cromanion_verify_claim.

secret.description: Shown ONCE. Store it now — we keep only its hash, so a lost secret means a new claim.

verifyUrl.description: The HTTP equivalent of cromanion_verify_claim, if you would rather curl it.
